Policy Name: Require a minimum number of reviewers
Definition: Requires approval from a specified minimum number of reviewers on pull requests before they can be completed. Supports options such as allowing requestors to approve their own changes, prohibiting the most recent pusher from approving, allowing completion even if some reviewers vote to wait or reject, and resetting votes when new changes are pushed.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Require a pull request before merging \u2013 ""Required number of approvals before merging""
GitHub Equivalent Description: Sets a required number of approving reviews before a PR can merge into the protected branch/ruleset target. Also supports dismissing stale approvals on new pushes (equivalent to reset-on-push, mapped separately below), requiring approval from someone other than the last pusher (equivalent to "prohibit most recent pusher"), and requiring reviews from Code Owners. Configurable via classic branch protection rules or the newer repository/organization rulesets.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Migrated automatically as "Required approving reviews.'' Verify branch patterns and the reviewer count after cutover.

Policy Name: Reset votes on new push (sub-setting of minimum reviewers)
Definition: Part of the minimum-reviewers policy: resets some or all approval votes whenever the source branch receives new commits, so stale approvals don't count toward completion.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Dismiss stale pull request approvals when new commits are pushed
GitHub Equivalent Description: A sub-option of "Require a pull request before merging" that automatically dismisses existing approvals when new commits change the PR diff, directly matching ADO's reset-votes-on-push behavior.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Migrated automatically as "Dismiss stale reviews.'' Confirm the setting is enabled on the protected branch/ruleset after migration.

Definition: Encourages traceability by checking that pull requests targeting the branch have at least one linked work item. Can be set as Required (blocking) or Optional (warning only).
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Require status checks to pass before merging (custom ""linked issue"" check)
GitHub Equivalent Description: GitHub has no native policy that requires a PR to reference/link a work item or Issue before merging. The closest equivalent is to add a required status check (e.g., a GitHub Action such as the community 'Require Linked Issue' action, or Actions that parse the PR body for closing keywords like 'Fixes #123') and mark that check as Required in a branch protection rule or ruleset. GitHub Projects/Issues linking itself is informational only and not enforced by branch protection.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Not migrated as an enforced policy. GitHub Enterprise Importer does migrate the underlying "work item links on pull requests'' as data/history, but there is no equivalent enforcement rule created automatically \u2013 build a custom status check if enforcement is required.

Definition: Checks that all comments/discussion threads on a pull request are resolved before the pull request can be completed. Can be set as Required (blocking) or Optional (warning only).
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Require conversation resolution before merging
GitHub Equivalent Description: Requires all review comment threads on a pull request to be marked resolved before the PR can be merged into the protected branch. Available in both classic branch protection rules and rulesets.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Not explicitly documented as an automated ado2gh mapping \u2013 verify manually and enable 'Require conversation resolution' post-migration if required.

Definition: Controls branch history by restricting which merge strategies (Basic merge/no fast-forward, Squash merge, Rebase and fast-forward, Rebase with merge commit) are allowed when completing pull requests into the branch.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: different granularity)
GitHub Documentation URL: Require a pull request before merging \u2013 ""Required merge method"" + Require linear history
GitHub Equivalent Description: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets#require-a-pull-request-before-merging
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Rulesets let you require a single merge method (merge commit, squash, or rebase) for PRs targeting the branch, combined with repository-level settings (Settings > General > Pull Requests) that enable/disable merge, squash, and rebase merging org/repo-wide. 'Require linear history' additionally blocks merge commits, similar to disallowing 'Basic merge (no fast-forward)' in Azure DevOps. GitHub allows enabling one required method via ruleset vs. ADO's multi-select allow-list of several strategies.
column10: Migrated automatically as "Allowed merge methods.'' Validate the merge settings (merge/squash/rebase) on the repository after migration.

Definition: Requires pull request changes to build successfully (via one or more configured build pipelines) before the pull request can complete. Supports automatic or manual trigger, required or optional enforcement, path filters, and build expiration settings.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Require status checks to pass before merging
GitHub Equivalent Description: Requires one or more CI checks (typically GitHub Actions workflow check runs) to report success before a PR can merge. Supports 'strict' (branch must be up to date) or 'loose' modes, similar to ADO's build-expiration/queue-on-source-update options. GitHub Actions plays the same role as Azure Pipelines build definitions here.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Migrated automatically as "Required status checks.'' Check names may need to be updated after pipelines are rewired from Azure Pipelines to GitHub Actions.

Policy Name: Status checks (Require approval from external services)
Definition: Allows external services to post detailed pass/fail status on pull requests via the Status API, and requires that status to succeed before the pull request can complete. Supports required or optional enforcement, authorized identity, reset conditions, policy applicability, and path filters.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Require status checks to pass before merging (Commit Status API / external checks)
GitHub Equivalent Description: GitHub uses the same 'Required status checks' mechanism for both CI builds and external service statuses posted via the Commit Status API or Checks API. You can restrict which GitHub App/service is allowed to set a given required status, analogous to ADO's 'authorized identity' setting.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Likely migrated automatically alongside Build validation as "Required status checks''; verify the external service/genre-name integration still posts statuses correctly after migration.

Definition: Automatically adds specified individuals or groups as reviewers on pull requests that change files in specified directories/paths (or all pull requests in the branch). Can be Required (their approval is mandatory) or Optional (added for visibility only).
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Require review from Code Owners (CODEOWNERS file)
GitHub Equivalent Description: GitHub achieves automatic/required path-based reviewers through a CODEOWNERS file that maps file/directory patterns to users or teams, combined with enabling 'Require review from Code Owners' in a branch protection rule or ruleset. Unlike ADO, GitHub Code Owners are always mandatory once the setting is enabled (no separate 'optional/visibility-only' mode), and up to 15 teams can specify required approval counts.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Not automatically migrated (manual). A CODEOWNERS file must be created (or an existing one validated) so its path entries match the same reviewer/path rules used in Azure DevOps.

Policy Name: Bypass policies when completing pull requests
Definition: A permission (not a toggleable policy setting) that allows designated users or groups to complete pull requests even if the pull request does not satisfy configured branch policies.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Ruleset bypass list / ""Do not allow bypassing the above settings""
GitHub Equivalent Description: Rulesets let you grant specific roles, teams, or apps permission to bypass some or all rules (including required reviews/status checks) when merging. Classic branch protection instead offers a single 'Do not allow bypassing the above settings' toggle that, by default, exempts admins/'bypass branch protections' role from all restrictions.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Not explicitly covered by the migration tool \u2013 reconfigure the ruleset/branch protection bypass list manually to match the intended bypass identities.

Definition: A permission (not a toggleable policy setting) that allows designated users or groups to push changes directly to a protected branch (from a local repo or the web) without satisfying configured branch policies.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Ruleset bypass list (applies to push-restricting rules) / ""Restrict who can push to matching branches""
GitHub Equivalent Description: Bypass actors configured on a ruleset can push directly to a protected branch even when rules like 'Require a pull request before merging' would otherwise block direct pushes. Classic branch protection's 'Restrict who can push to matching branches' plus the default admin exemption provide the equivalent control.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Not explicitly covered by the migration tool \u2013 reconfigure the ruleset/branch protection bypass list manually to match the intended bypass identities.

Definition: A repository-level policy that blocks pushes containing commits whose author email address does not match one or more specified patterns.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Commit author email pattern restriction (ruleset metadata restriction) / Require signed commits
GitHub Equivalent Description: GitHub rulesets support a commit-metadata restriction that can require commit author emails to match a pattern (for example, ending in a specific domain), which is the direct analog of ADO's policy. 'Require signed commits' is a complementary but distinct control that verifies cryptographic identity rather than matching an email string. Note: GitHub's official migration guidance warns that org-level rulesets requiring a specific author-email pattern can cause a repository migration to fail outright if existing commits don't already comply.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Partially supported by GitHub Enterprise Importer as "Commit email pattern checks.'' Review and adjust the patterns after migration to match your original policy intent, and confirm existing commit history complies before migrating.

Definition: A repository-level policy that blocks pushes that introduce file paths matching one or more specified (blocked) patterns.
Mapping Type: Exact (1:1) as a GitHub feature; No Direct Equivalent in automated migration
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Restrict file paths (ruleset rule)
GitHub Equivalent Description: A repository or organization ruleset rule that blocks pushes containing files/paths matching specified fnmatch patterns (up to 200 entries), with support for allowed exceptions. Directly equivalent in capability to ADO's file path validation patterns, but must be configured manually after migration.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: No direct equivalent is created automatically by the migration tool. Resolve any path/name restrictions before migrating, then manually configure a 'Restrict file paths' ruleset rule to match the original ADO policy.

Definition: A repository-level policy that switches the repository from case-sensitive to case-insensitive (Windows/macOS-friendly) mode, blocking pushes that introduce files, folders, branches, or tags differing only by letter casing.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: None \u2013 not available as a native GitHub setting
GitHub Equivalent Description: GitHub has no built-in toggle to enforce case-insensitive naming across files, folders, branches, or tags. There is no rule in the available rulesets list or repository settings that corresponds to this. Teams typically rely on client-side Git configuration (`core.ignorecase`), linting/CI checks, or a custom required status check/Action to catch case-only naming collisions before merge.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: No direct equivalent. Resolve any case-sensitivity conflicts (duplicate names differing only by case) in the repository before migrating, since GitHub cannot enforce or auto-correct this afterward.

Definition: A repository-level policy that blocks pushes containing file or folder names that are invalid/reserved on one or more major operating systems (Windows, macOS, Linux), preventing working directory corruption on those platforms.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Restrict file paths (ruleset rule
GitHub Equivalent Description: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets#restrict-file-paths
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: GitHub has no dedicated 'reserved/invalid OS names' rule like ADO's built-in cross-platform name list. The closest approach is to manually enumerate reserved names (e.g., CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9, trailing dot/space) as fnmatch patterns in a 'Restrict file paths' ruleset rule, or enforce via a custom required status check/Action.
column10: No direct equivalent is created automatically by the migration tool. Resolve any reserved/invalid file or folder names in the repository before migrating to meet GitHub's cross-platform naming limits.

Definition: A repository-level policy that blocks pushes containing file or directory paths exceeding a specified maximum length, avoiding path-length incompatibilities across operating systems.
Mapping Type: Exact (1:1) as a GitHub feature; No Direct Equivalent in automated migration
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Restrict file path length (ruleset rule) / 255-byte Git reference name limit
GitHub Equivalent Description: A repository or organization ruleset rule that blocks pushes containing file paths exceeding a configured character limit \u2013 directly equivalent in capability to ADO's maximum path length policy. Separately, GitHub enforces a hard, non-configurable 255-byte limit on Git reference (branch/tag) names.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: No direct equivalent is created automatically by the migration tool. Resolve path length issues before migrating to meet GitHub's limits (255-byte ref names), then manually configure a 'Restrict file path length' ruleset rule if you want to keep enforcing it going forward.

Definition: A repository-level policy that blocks pushes containing new or updated files larger than a specified size limit, helping to prevent bloated repositories and slow clone times.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Restrict file size (ruleset rule)
GitHub Equivalent Description: A repository or organization ruleset rule that blocks pushes containing files exceeding a configured size limit, with support for allowed exceptions (e.g., Gradle wrapper JARs). Directly equivalent to ADO's maximum file size policy. GitHub also enforces a hard 100 MiB per-file limit post-migration (400 MiB during migration) regardless of ruleset configuration, and offers a related 'Restrict file extensions' rule with no direct ADO counterpart.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Migrated automatically as "Max file size.'' Large files that exceed GitHub's 100 MiB per-file limit may require Git LFS (future work) or Git history cleanup before/after migration.

Definition: Allows branch policies (minimum reviewers, work item linking, comment resolution, build validation, etc.) to be applied to a specific branch name or the default branch across all repositories in a project simultaneously, rather than repository-by-repository.
Mapping Type: Exact (1:1) as a GitHub feature; Not migrated automatically
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Organization-level rulesets
GitHub Equivalent Description: Organization rulesets apply a single set of branch/tag rules (reviews, status checks, merge restrictions, path/size restrictions, etc.) across some or all repositories in an organization by targeting repository name patterns or properties, matching ADO's cross-repository branch policy scope.
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Not migrated. GitHub Enterprise Importer explicitly excludes user-scoped and cross-repo branch policies from migration; recreate this behavior manually as an organization-level ruleset after migration.

Policy Type: Branch Behavior (Implicit \u2013 not a named ADO UI policy)
Definition: Automatically enforced by Azure DevOps once any branch policy is configured on a branch: prevents force pushes (history rewrites) to that branch.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Block force pushes (ruleset rule
GitHub Equivalent Description: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets#block-force-pushes
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Prevents force pushes to the targeted branches or tags; enabled by default in rulesets, and also configurable in classic branch protection rules ('Allow force pushes' toggle, off by default).
column10: Migrated automatically as "Block force pushes.'' Confirm enforcement is active on the protected branch/ruleset after migration.

Policy Type: Branch Behavior (Implicit \u2013 not a named ADO UI policy)
Definition: Automatically enforced by Azure DevOps once any branch policy is configured on a branch: prevents the branch from being deleted while policies are active.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Restrict deletions (ruleset rule
GitHub Equivalent Description: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets#restrict-deletions
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Only users with bypass permissions can delete branches or tags matching the ruleset pattern; selected by default. Classic branch protection has an equivalent 'Allow deletions' toggle (off by default).
column10: Migrated automatically as "Restrict deletions.'' Confirm branch deletion is blocked where required after migration.

Policy Type: PR Workflow Setting (not a named Branch Policies-page policy)
Definition: A pull request completion option in Azure DevOps that automatically completes the PR as soon as all required policies pass, without further manual action.
GitHub Equivalent Policy Name: Auto-merge
GitHub Equivalent Description: GitHub's auto-merge is enabled per pull request (not as a repository-wide default) and automatically merges once all required reviews and status checks pass. Behavior differs from ADO's auto-complete in scope and configuration model (per-PR opt-in vs. a branch-level expectation).
GitHub Enterprise Importer (ado2gh) Migr: Not a branch policy migrated by the tool. GitHub auto-merge must be enabled per pull request going forward; validate this matches your preferred workflow after migration.
